claims.text: Local nanoscale phase heterogeneity governs the strong low-field magnetocaloric response of the rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy.
Nanoscale phase heterogeneity creates regions of enhanced magnetostructural coupling.
Nanoscale phase heterogeneity creates spatial variability in magnetic exchange.
The proposed nanoscale heterogeneity permits rapid thermal exchange while retaining a strong magnetocaloric response.
The proposed nanoscale heterogeneity permits low hysteresis and mechanical stability.
The as-cast alloy has inherent chemical disorder and microscale compositional fluctuations.
Controlled annealing can partially homogenize the local chemical and phase distribution without completely eliminating nanoscale heterogeneity.
Nanoscale phase boundaries and local chemical inhomogeneities mediate magnetostructural coupling.
Nanoscale heterogeneous regions enhance magnetoelastic effects.
Enhanced magnetoelastic effects in the nanoscale regions produce localized magnetic entropy changes.
Localized magnetic entropy changes facilitate a strong magnetocaloric response at applied fields below 1 T.
Annealed samples with optimized nanoscale heterogeneity will have a larger magnetic entropy change than the as-cast baseline at low applied fields.
Annealed samples with optimized nanoscale heterogeneity will maintain or improve heat-transfer rates relative to the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples with optimized nanoscale heterogeneity will exhibit less magnetic-cycling hysteresis than the as-cast baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies to chemically complex high-entropy-alloy compositions having roughly 10% local compositional variation.
The proposed mechanism applies below 1 T and around room temperature.
